C-39.IntentSummary: Tables: default rendering that never overflows the text column (scroll wrapper + edge shadows, content width, long-token wrap, PDF/HTML export rules), session-only column resize, and the fullscreen viewer shared with C-34 R2.2 (tracked as C-34 T-002). T-001.Title: T1 default table rendering: scroll wrapper + edge shadows, content width, long-token wrap, export/PDF rules

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A 15-column table stays inside the text column and scrolls horizontally; an edge shadow marks the side with hidden columns (start/end), updated on scroll and resize.
Body cells wrap unbreakable tokens (max ≈ 40ch, overflow-wrap: anywhere); header cells do not break mid-word.
Table editing inside the wrapper still works: cell focus/caret, drag bars (left/bottom handlers), table tools toolbar, cell selection, row/column insert.
HTML export and print/PDF: no scroll container; wide tables wrap so every column is visible.
Unit/e2e pins (Chromium + WebKit): wrapper scrollWidth > clientWidth for the wide table, table width == content for the narrow table, URL cell does not exceed the cap.

Verification.Command: npm run build && npx playwright test tests/e2e/table-layout.spec.ts

T-002.Title: T3 session-only column resize

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Dragging a column border resizes live; the saved markdown is byte-identical; reload restores auto layout; double-click resets.

T-002.Notes: 2026-10-15: implemented as muya.tableResize (src/muya/lib/tableResize/). Identity = the table block key (the table element's DOM id): stable across re-renders, survives tab switches because tab activation restores the saved block tree (same keys), and is minted fresh by every re-parse, so a disk reload / close+reopen can never pick up stale widths. Widths ride in the table vnode (colgroup + table.ag-column-widths-fixed + inline width), so every muya render re-applies them by construction; render/partialRender/singleRender additionally call reconcileAfterRender next to the T-001 scroll restore for column-count changes (surviving widths keep their index, new columns get their measured auto width) and for widths a hidden render could not measure. First drag freezes the auto layout as the baseline (fixed layout needs a width for every column); min 48px; double-click resets that column (measured natural width, or the whole table back to auto when no manual column remains); a click on the handle without a move un-freezes again. Handles are invisible span.ag-column-resizer zones on each th's right border (last column inside the box so the wrapper scroll range is unchanged), accent-coloured hairline on hover/drag, capture-phase pointer interaction with pointer capture so muya's caret/cell-selection handlers never see the gesture. Not available on the read-only Split View mirror (options.disableTableColumnResize, set from the mirror prop in editor.vue); reading/locked tabs keep it (view-only). The fullscreen block viewer shows the session widths (clone keeps the colgroup) without handles. Markdown/undo/isSaved/export/print are untouched by construction (nothing in the path calls contentState). Tests: tests/renderer/muya/table-column-resize.test.js (store, clamp, reconcile, vnodes, real-Muya render + markdown/history identity) and tests/e2e/table-column-resize.spec.ts in the chromium and webkit-tables projects (new playwright project; also brings table-layout.spec.ts into WebKit).

Red on main: table-column-resize.test.js fails to load; the e2e fails 6/8 (caret-near-border guard and one geometry check pass by design). WebKit screenshots: accent hairline while dragging, widths kept after release, header border intact. webkit-tables (and webkit-mica from T-007) added to the CI WebKit step.
